What it would do differently

The leads the player wrote, each with where it happened and what would settle it. An ask is a link into the replay above.

  1. Does the SQUARE_DTRAP flag really stop every run, or only a pathfind?

    run_step is shared by . (run) and the pathfind, so both should stop.

    What would settle it: one run that casts Find Traps and then compares a .-run and a g-pathfind over the same stretch of the same level.

  2. How far can a mage get with one Find Traps cast?

    The window is ±22 rows and ±40 columns on a 198×66 level, so one cast covers 28 % of it, and the dtrap block is 81×45. My guess is "the whole way, in one ask".

    What would settle it: a mage that casts once and then walks a known route inside the block, measuring how many tiles the walk covers in one ask when the path never leaves the block.

  3. Is l> cheaper than M for locating a remembered staircase?

    M draws the whole remembered level in one ask and the staircase is visible in it, but M is scaled 2.5× and I could not plan a route from it. l> gives an exact tile offset.

    What would settle it: a run that presses M and then l>, and reports whether the two agree.

  4. Is Magic Missile worth more than a second Phase Door scroll for a character at depth 2?

    I chose Magic Missile and it killed a centipede in one cast that no flask could have touched (AC 4 would have been easy, but Fang at AC 36 was not).

    What would settle it: a run that fights Fang on depth 2 with Magic Missile and measures how many spell points it takes to kill 25 hit points of AC 36.

  5. Is a yellow mushroom patch worth killing rather than avoiding?

    It has 1 HP and AC 1, so one oil flask kills it, and it did terrify me for 3–4 turns.

    What would settle it: a run that measures how often the patches are on the path of the staircase.

- Files I actually opened before my first keypress: manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md (all 232 lines), agents/minimax/COMMON.md (all 380), agents/minimax/DRUID.md (all 315), docs/BRIEF.md, records/OVERVIEW.md (to pick an unused seed), vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/class.txt (Mage block) and p_race.txt (Gnome block). I did NOT read knowledge/*.md or any other run's decisions. Seed chosen: 41 (seeds already in use: 7, 11, 23, 103). (ask 1)
- Mage's CL1 spell Find Traps, Doors & Stairs = DETECT_TRAPS/DOORS/STAIRS with effect-yx:22:40; src/effect-handler-general.c:1467 DETECT_STAIRS scans the real grid (not the remembered map) and calls square_memorize + square_light_spot on every stair square in the window, so it reveals the down staircase even if never seen. The mage's answer to the staircase hunt that cost every earlier run a hundred asks. (ask 10)
- The town of Angband 4.2.6 has a down staircase on the north wall and the player is PLACED ON IT: src/gen-cave.c town_gen_layout ends with square_set_feat(c, pgrid, FEAT_MORE) then player_place(c, p, pgrid). The status line already says 'Down staircase' in town, so '>' should go straight to depth 1 - no staircase hunt for the first level. (ask 11)
- Buying in Angband 4.2.6 is ONE ask: 'p' then the row letter, then the quantity digits, then Enter, then ANY key to accept. src/ui-store.c store_purchase: after get_quantity it prints 'Price: N' at row 1 and asks 'Buy <item>? [ESC, any other key to accept]' via store_get_check. The Enter is consumed by the quantity string prompt, so a confirmation key is still needed - that is why 'p' + 'j' + '20' + Enter alone leaves gold unchanged. (ask 14)
- Armour display in Angband 4.2.6 shops is [AC,to-armour]: Metal Scale Mail [38,+0] matches the classic AC 38, Soft Leather Armour [8,+1] is AC 8. So the first number is real armour class and the sheet line 'Armor [%d,%+d]' is [protection, AC] (src/ui-player.c:735). For a Gnome Mage with 8 HP, AC is the best gold there is: Soft Leather 104g + Metal Cap 24g + Cloak 6g = AC 12. (ask 17)
- TRAP: when a store item sells out, the whole list RENUMBERS and every letter below it changes (Soft Leather was f, so the Wicker Shields moved from m to j, Metal Caps from r to q). Read the letter off the screen again after every purchase - the letter is a label, and buying shifts the labels. (ask 18)
- The hit formula in 4.2.6 (src/player-attack.c:196 hit_chance) is hit% = 12 + 83*(to_hit - 2*AC/3)/to_hit with a 5% always-miss. So AC 12 needs to_hit>=8 and AC 20 needs to_hit>=13: a monster below to_hit 13 cannot touch me at all. With 8 HP that is the difference between one fight and three. (ask 19)
- Equip in REVERSE pack-letter order (n, m, i, g): removing an item renumbers the pack letters, but only the letters AFTER the removed one move, so taking the last one first leaves every earlier letter valid. The pack skips h, j, k, l, so 10 items are a b c d e f g i m n. (ask 24)
- Where the down staircase is: src/gen-util.c alloc_stairs() picks a random EMPTY floor square with exactly 3 adjacent walls (a dead-end corridor), reducing to 2,1,0 walls only if none exists; src/gen-cave.c handle_level_stairs() sets minsep = MIN(width,height)/4 = 16, so the down staircase is more than 16 tiles away from the up staircase in x or y. The level is the full 198x66 (classic_gen does cave_new(dungeon_hgt, dungeon_wid)). (ask 46)
- HARNESS TRAP (mine, cost 5 asks): the frontend (patch/src/main-agent.c) drops a TRAILING LITERAL NEWLINE in the keys file, so a last key sent as a real newline byte is silently lost. Write the two-character escape \n instead of a real newline - in bash that means double quotes "\n", NOT $'\n'. With a dropped Enter the rest prompt sat open and every key after it was eaten by the prompt. Also: the game can be left sitting in the LOOK/TARGETING mode ('Press '?' for help.' at the bottom of the screen); press Escape before any other command. (ask 72)
- Aiming the cursor at an UNKNOWN square gives a bogus short path (find_path with only_known=false assumes unknown squares are passable and the reconstructed path can be nonsense - aim-20 gave 0 steps, aim-3 gave 3). Aiming at a KNOWN square gives a proper known-only path and a long walk. Use known landmarks (stairs, doors you have seen) as aiming points. (ask 90)
- OBSERVED (minimaxflash-2, asks 72-109): the Find Traps/Doors/Doors & Stairs spell only reports NEW squares - casting it again from within 10 tiles of the previous cast says 'You sense no traps. You sense no doors.' even though the window is the same. So the spell is a scanner of UNSCANNED area, and to widen the search the mage must MOVE between casts (the DETECT effects memorise what they find, so a second cast over the same window finds nothing new). Also: casting Find Traps from a spot where no stair is in the 81x45 window (the code scans player->grid.y +/- 22 and player->grid.x +/- 40) prints NO message at all about stairs - the DETECT_STAIRS handler only says 'You sense no stairs.' when context->aware is set, so silence means 'no stairs here' but you cannot tell it apart from 'the message was overwritten'. (ask 109)

- ROOT CAUSE OF THE BROKEN WALKS (my prior life's 11 Find Traps casts): src/effect-handler-general.c:1376 sets SQUARE_DTRAP on EVERY square in the +-22 x +-40 DETECT_TRAPS window, whether or not a trap is there. src/cmd-cave.c:1146-1153 then does disturb() whenever a run or pathfind steps OFF a dtrap square (old_dtrap && !new_dtrap, and running_firststep exempts only the first step). So one Find Traps cast blanks a 81x45 region with a flag that makes the game's own pathfinder walk stop after one step. The fix costs one spell point: cast it again from a position whose window covers the whole path, and the seams between separate casts are welded shut. (ask 258)

note: Buying in Angband 4.2.6 is ONE ask: 'p' then the row letter, then the quantity digits, then Enter, then ANY key to accept. src/ui-store.c store_purchase: after get_quantity it prints 'Price: N' at row 1 and asks 'Buy <item>? [ESC, any other key to accept]' via store_get_check. The Enter is consumed by the quantity string prompt, so a confirmation key is still needed - that is why 'p' + 'j' + '20' + Enter alone leaves gold unchanged. (ask 14)

note: Armour display in Angband 4.2.6 shops is [AC,to-armour]: Metal Scale Mail [38,+0] matches the classic AC 38, Soft Leather Armour [8,+1] is AC 8. So the first number is real armour class and the sheet line 'Armor [%d,%+d]' is [protection, AC] (src/ui-player.c:735). For a Gnome Mage with 8 HP, AC is the best gold there is: Soft Leather 104g + Metal Cap 24g + Cloak 6g = AC 12. (ask 17)

note: The hit formula in 4.2.6 (src/player-attack.c:196 hit_chance) is hit% = 12 + 83*(to_hit - 2*AC/3)/to_hit with a 5% always-miss. So AC 12 needs to_hit>=8 and AC 20 needs to_hit>=13: a monster below to_hit 13 cannot touch me at all. With 8 HP that is the difference between one fight and three. (ask 19)

note: HARNESS TRAP (mine, cost 5 asks): the frontend (patch/src/main-agent.c) drops a TRAILING LITERAL NEWLINE in the keys file, so a last key sent as a real newline byte is silently lost. Write the two-character escape \n instead of a real newline - in bash that means double quotes "\n", NOT $'\n'. With a dropped Enter the rest prompt sat open and every key after it was eaten by the prompt. Also: the game can be left sitting in the LOOK/TARGETING mode ('Press '?' for help.' at the bottom of the screen); press Escape before any other command. (ask 72)

note: OBSERVED (minimaxflash-2, asks 72-109): the Find Traps/Doors/Doors & Stairs spell only reports NEW squares - casting it again from within 10 tiles of the previous cast says 'You sense no traps. You sense no doors.' even though the window is the same. So the spell is a scanner of UNSCANNED area, and to widen the search the mage must MOVE between casts (the DETECT effects memorise what they find, so a second cast over the same window finds nothing new). Also: casting Find Traps from a spot where no stair is in the 81x45 window (the code scans player->grid.y +/- 22 and player->grid.x +/- 40) prints NO message at all about stairs - the DETECT_STAIRS handler only says 'You sense no stairs.' when context->aware is set, so silence means 'no stairs here' but you cannot tell it apart from 'the message was overwritten'. (ask 109)

note: ROOT CAUSE OF THE BROKEN WALKS (my prior life's 11 Find Traps casts): src/effect-handler-general.c:1376 sets SQUARE_DTRAP on EVERY square in the +-22 x +-40 DETECT_TRAPS window, whether or not a trap is there. src/cmd-cave.c:1146-1153 then does disturb() whenever a run or pathfind steps OFF a dtrap square (old_dtrap && !new_dtrap, and running_firststep exempts only the first step). So one Find Traps cast blanks a 81x45 region with a flag that makes the game's own pathfinder walk stop after one step. The fix costs one spell point: cast it again from a position whose window covers the whole path, and the seams between separate casts are welded shut. (ask 258)
